deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen is moderately constructive: 70 names (20 strong buys, 50 buys) versus 43 avoids, with the bulk of the universe (136) on hold. Among the five highest-ranked strong buys, two are Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group), with one each in Healthcare, Communication Services, and Agriculture/Commodities — a value tilt toward cyclical and yield-oriented names rather than a single-sector cluster. Several top names were downgraded from strong buy to buy by overlay flags (earnings-basis divergence, FCF basis mismatch, or interim-quality concerns), so headline signals overstate conviction. All five picks are new (one week at signal) with conviction scores of 38–50%, and FCF/earnings basis figures often disagree across filing, TTM, and company-adjusted sources — treat cheapness and yield metrics as provisional until reconciled.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Flagged on cheapness and cash generation: 11/22 models passed (composite 92%, sector-relative 86%) across all five factor families, with standout passes on Earnings Yield (E/P 10.9%, P/E 9.2), FCF Yield (37.2%), Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality. Failures cluster on balance-sheet quality: Financial Health (D/E 161%, current ratio 0.73), Graham Enterprising (excessive leverage, negative earnings growth −5.9%), Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat. Industrials concentration applies alongside MEGP.L. **Verdict: watchlist** — headline value is compelling, but high leverage, weak liquidity, statutory earnings decline, and a flagged FCF basis mismatch (filing $362.6M vs screen TTM $302.8M vs company-adj £113.5M) warrant reconciliation before sizing.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Strongest model breadth after AEP.L: 15/22 passes (composite 84%, sector-relative 89%) including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield (P/E 7.8, E/P 12.8%), FCF Yield (5.7%), Buffett Quality, Economic Moat (ROE 28.2%), High Dividend Yield (6.9%), Magic Formula, and Financial Health (D/E 28%). Piotroski F-Score failed at 6/9 (ROA and asset turnover not improving); Earnings Quality failed on weak free-cash conversion. Interim-quality and earnings-basis overlays adjusted the signal to Buy. Shares another Industrials slot with FGP.L. **Verdict: watchlist** — quantitative profile is attractive on valuation and quality screens, but interim EPS decline, FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (per overlay), and statutory earnings growth of −3.9% need confirmation.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — 10/22 models passed (composite 80%, sector-relative 90%) on quality and income: Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Composite Value, and Financial Health (D/E 77%, CR 1.82). Cheapness screens largely failed — Earnings Yield (7.9% < 8%), FCF Yield (3.5% < 5%), Low P/E + High Yield (P/E 12.6 not below 12) — and Piotroski scored 6/9 with leverage not declining. Healthcare diversifies sector exposure. FCF basis overlay flags filing $119M vs screen TTM $14.4M; OCF fell from $564M to $436M YoY. **Verdict: watchlist** — sector-relative ranking is strong, but sub-5% FCF yield, weak cash conversion, negative statutory earnings growth (−4.7%), and extreme FCF divergence limit confidence in reported cheapness.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Broad cheapness and income pass set: 15/22 models (composite 76%, sector-relative 86%) including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (5.5%), Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.45, growth 26.7%), High Dividend Yield (6.8%), Dividend Growth, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (D/E 52%). Quality screens failed: Buffett Quality (ROE 13.5%, thin margins), Economic Moat, and critically Piotroski F-Score at 3/9 (ROA, OCF > NI, leverage, margins, and turnover all failing). FCF basis overlay shows filing $148M vs screen TTM $211.9M vs company-adj £325M. Price is below the 200-day MA with RSI 37. **Verdict: watchlist** — income and growth metrics screen well, but the 3/9 Piotroski score and wide FCF definition spread suggest deteriorating operational momentum masked by headline yield.

**AEP.L (AEP Plantations Plc)** — Cleanest quantitative profile: 18/22 models passed (composite 82%, conviction 50%) including both Graham Defensive and Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (12.4%), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield (5.6%), Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (D/E ~0%, current ratio 8.69). Only four failures: Graham Net-Net (no NCAV), Schloss/Deep Value (P/B 1.6), Lynch PEG (PEG 1.38). No overlay downgrades; adjusted signal remains strong buy. Sole Agriculture/Commodities name among top five. **Verdict: accumulate** — widest model agreement, fortress balance sheet, and no basis or quality overlays make this the most actionable name, pending commodity-cycle diligence.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 161%) and weak liquidity (CR 0.73) are screen-visible but contract-renewal risk, pension obligations, and UK transport regulatory/policy shifts are not captured; open question on whether post-privatisation cash flows are structurally sustainable.
- FGP.L: Statutory earnings growth −5.9% vs adjusted +16% — governance/earnings-quality concern around adjustment items not fully explained in the screen.
- MEGP.L: Interim EPS decline and FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (overlay) raise dividend sustainability risk; cyclical exposure to discretionary consumer/travel photography spend is not modelled.
- MEGP.L: Statutory earnings growth −3.9% with 6.9% yield — open question on whether the dividend is fully covered by recurring FCF.
- HIK.L: Generic pharmaceutical pricing/regulatory risk (FDA, US Medicaid, UK NHS) and patent-cliff dynamics are absent from the screen; open question on pipeline replacing mature product cash flows.
- HIK.L: OCF declined from $564M to $436M and FCF from $329M to $119M — cyclical or one-off drivers unclear from JSON alone.
- ITV.L: Structural decline in linear-TV advertising share and streaming competition are not quantified; 6.8% yield with Piotroski 3/9 raises governance/capital-allocation concern if dividend is prioritised over reinvestment.
- ITV.L: FCF figures range from $148M (filing) to £325M (company-adj) — open question on which basis reflects maintainable free cash flow for shareholders.
- AEP.L: Timber/plantation commodity cyclicality and climate/biological asset impairment risk are not in the screen; open question on how sensitive earnings are to log-price cycles despite near-zero leverage.
- AEP.L: Adjusted EPS growth (+35.8%) far exceeds statutory (+7.5%) — open question on one-off gains in plantation valuations or harvest timing.
deep_analysis.red_flags:
## NAMES WORTH DEEPER RESEARCH

- AEP.L — Which FCF and earnings basis (statutory vs adjusted) reflects normalised harvest economics, and how correlated is the dividend to timber/log-price cycles?
- FGP.L — Can company-adjusted FCF of £113.5M be reconciled with filing $362.6M, and is the 160% D/E ratio serviceable through the contract portfolio without covenant or refinancing stress?
- ITV.L — Is the 6.8% dividend sustainable on filing-aligned FCF ($148M), and what is the credible path for advertising revenue as viewing shifts away from linear broadcast?

documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary: FirstGroup is a UK-focused public transport operator (First Bus, First Rail open access and DfT-contracted rail, Rail Services) that has repositioned after exiting North America. The quantitative screen rates it a **strong buy** (11/22 models; composite 92%), driven by cheapness (P/E 9.2, earnings yield ~11%), high reported FCF yield, dividend growth, and Piotroski F-Score 8/9. Filings show a credible earnings trajectory: FY 2025 adjusted EPS rose 16% to 19.4p on £1.37bn adjusted revenue; H1 FY 2026 adjusted EPS was 9.9p (+16%) with management guiding modest full-year EPS growth. The valuation hook is a cash-generative, buyback-active name (new £100m programme announced June 2026) trading below typical quality multiples, with open-access rail and bus M&A as growth offsets to DfT TOC nationalisation. The key debate is whether screen-level FCF and low P/E fully reflect elevated leverage (D/E ~161%, current ratio 0.73), statutory/adjusted earnings divergence, and structural bus volume pressure (£3 fare cap, NI costs) plus rail contract roll-off.
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a business that has materially improved since the North American disposals: FY 2025 adjusted operating profit reached £222.8m (+9%) and free cash flow £113.5m (Annual Report 2025 / FY 2025 results presentation), with adjusted net debt of £86.9m and progressive dividends (6.5p total). Capital returns are active—£92m buybacks in FY 2025, £50m completed in H1 FY 2026, plus a £100m programme launched June 2026 (RNS headline; body not extracted).

Quality markers supporting the screen include: (1) **five model families passed**—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk; (2) **Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman, Composite Value, Earnings Quality** all passing; (3) **dividend growth** with ~3.9% yield; (4) **ROE 16.7%** though below moat thresholds. Management is deliberately diversifying: First Bus London (~£150m H1 revenue), Business & Coach, open-access rail expansion (c.£500m Hitachi fleet order; capacity set to more than double), London Overground contract (mobilisation from May 2026), and bolt-on coach acquisitions.

For a value investor, the case is a **transition play at a discount**: earnings and cash conversion have improved, the balance sheet target is <2.0x adjusted net debt/EBITDA, and ~£125m TOC transition cash is expected over three years as National Rail Contracts transfer to public ownership—partially replacing fee income with capital return. The screen’s FCF-basis overlay (filing $362.6m vs company-adjusted £113.5m) warrants caution but does not invalidate the cheapness signal if adjusted metrics and bus/rail pipeline deliver as guided.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a global estate of ~49,000 self-service vending units, led by Photo.ME photobooths and the fast-growing Wash.ME laundry franchise across 16 countries. FY2025 delivered record profit before tax of £78.2m on £315.4m revenue, with laundry now contributing 46% of group EBITDA; the quantitative screen flags a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 7.8, yield 6.9%), quality (ROE 28.2%) and balance-sheet strength (net cash £26.5m at October 2025). The central debate is whether laundry rollout and capital returns (8.64p total dividend, £18m buyback) outweigh a revised FY2026 PBT range of £69–74m, April trading softness in France, German photo-ID regulation, and weaker interim cash conversion. Filings are comprehensive for FY2025 annual and H1 2026 interim; `macro_context.json` is absent from the source pack.
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal (15/22 models passing; composite 84%; families: cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) aligns with a business that combines dominant site-owner relationships, high EBITDA margins (~38%), and a visible growth engine in Wash.ME. FY2025 RNS results show revenue +2.4% to £315.4m, EBITDA +5.4% to £120.4m, cash from operations +8.9% to £115.5m, and diluted EPS +4.5% to 14.91p — consistent with the screen’s quality and dividend passes (Buffett Quality, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Financial Health).

The value case rests on three pillars visible in filings rather than screens alone. First, structural mix shift: laundry revenue rose 17.3% to £112.4m with 1,145 net machine additions; Wash.ME EBITDA margin was 49.4%. Second, capital discipline with optionality: net cash of £26.5m (excluding £13.0m lease liabilities), capex guided at £57–59m for FY2026, and a £18m share buyback launched March 2026. Third, shareholder returns: total dividend increased 9.5% to 8.64p (58% of EPS), policy targeting >55% of profit after tax.

Why strong buy for a value investor: low multiple on a cash-generative, asset-backed vending model with barriers to entry (long-term site contracts; no customer >2% of turnover). The screen’s adjusted signal (Buy, not Strong Buy) correctly flags interim friction — H1 2026 PBT −3.8%, interim dividend cut to 3.60p, and FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× — but does not invalidate the underlying franchise. At ~11% below the 200-day moving average with neutral RSI (54), timing is unexciting but not adverse for a patient accumulator.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma is a diversified multinational generics and branded-pharmaceuticals group with roughly 60% of revenue in North America, a leading MENA Branded franchise, and investment-grade balance sheet (BBB/stable, S&P and Fitch). The quantitative screen flags a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 12.6, P/B 1.9), quality (ROE 15.4%), dividend (3.8% yield), and financial health, with 10 of 22 models passing at an 80% composite score. The valuation hook is a FTSE 100-quality cash-generative pharma name trading below mid-teens earnings after a February 2026 de-rating, now recovering on a solid H1 2026 beat and active $250m buyback. The key debate is whether Branded and Hikma Rx momentum can offset Injectables margin erosion, weak reported free-cash conversion, and rising leverage (net debt/core EBITDA 1.9x at H1 2026), or whether withdrawn medium-term guidance signals a structurally lower earnings trajectory.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination of screen-passing valuation, visible capital return, and business quality across three distinct segments. The screen passes five metric families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — with Graham Enterprising, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, and Financial Health among the ten passing models. Debt/equity of 77% and a current ratio of 1.8 sit within conservative thresholds, while ROE of 15.4% and a 3.8% dividend yield support the quality and income case.

Business quality is anchored in segment diversification. Branded (MENA) delivered 10% revenue growth and 19% core operating profit growth in FY2025, accelerating to 15% revenue and 23% core profit growth in H1 2026. Hikma Rx generated over $1bn in core revenue with improving margins (core operating margin 17.3% in FY2025, 20.6% in H1 2026). Injectables remains the US hospital injectables leader by volume but is in a deliberate reinvestment phase, with core margin guided down to 27–28% for 2026 from 31.0% in FY2025.

Capital allocation reinforces the case: total dividend rose 5% to 84 cents in FY2025, interim dividend up 6% to 38 cents in H1 2026, and $227m of the $250m buyback was executed by 5 August 2026. ROIC of 16.0% (FY2025 filing) and trailing core EBITDA of $887m (H1 2026 filing) support returns above the cost of capital despite statutory earnings noise from legal settlements.

The screen’s adjusted Buy (from Strong Buy) reflects two overlays worth heeding: statutory EPS growth is slightly negative (-4.7%) while adjusted EPS growth is positive (+1.7%), and FCF basis divergence (filing-aligned FCF $119m vs screen TTM $14.4m) causes FCF Yield and Earnings Quality models to fail. These do not invalidate the value case but argue for staged accumulation rather than full conviction at screen weight.

documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced — pricing, regulatory, pipeline (partially closed):**
- Principal risks explicitly cover pricing/reimbursement, regulatory policy, and IP (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`).
- Structural US generic pricing pressure: Hikma Rx "modest"/"usual" price erosion (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`, `ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`); FY2026 sodium oxybate competition expected with partial mix mitigation.
- Product-specific cliff proxies (not patent-dated): US competition on testosterone and calcitonin; authorised generic sodium oxybate still contributing but flagged for future competition (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`, `ir_a70365d580129295.txt`).
- US import tariffs on generics monitored; company cites majority US-manufactured sales as mitigation (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); China-to-US tariff impact ~$3m in FY2025 (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`).
- Pipeline activity credible (118 Injectables products FY2025; 212/131/58 programmes per H1 presentation) but Bedford revenue deferred to 2028; withdrawn medium-term margin guidance leaves replacement timing uncertain.

**Still open — payer and patent quantification:**
- Medicaid, NHS, and FDA Orange Book expiry schedules absent from all 38 body extracts. **Next source:** FDA Orange Book + NHS Drug Tariff crosswalk against disclosed top products (US wholesalers each 11% of H1 revenue).

**Evidenced — other (unchanged from prior pass):**
- Injectables margin compression (guided 27–28% for 2026); leverage 1.9x; MENA geopolitical/shipping cost inflation (`94eb1f8d38a51fa6.txt`); CFO transition ongoing; customer concentration (two US wholesalers at 11% each).

**Capital return:** Sustained buyback activity — “Hikma Pharmaceuticals (HIK) Buys Back 569,511 Shares in Week Ending 7 August 2026 as Part of $250 Million Repurchase Plan” (Kalkine Media, 10 Aug 2026).

**Regulatory/legal:** Supreme Court ruled in Hikma’s favour dismissing Amarin skinny-label litigation (H1 2026 interim filing).

**Shareholder flows:** Wellington Management reduced stake below 5% threshold (Kalkine Media, 24 Jul 2026).
